why_it_matters: A pharmacovigilance program that applies objective study validity diagnostics before unblinding; the abstract reports that 26 of 110 evaluations failed them and were not unblinded. Shows the gate working at scale.

Defines staging (feasibility and bias checks before the comparative analysis) and a clean room (restricted access, deviation policy, audit trail) with a masked review team. cleanTMLE follows its stages and exports its Table S1 columns.

short_title: Evolocumab cohort with controls before outcome analysis
why_it_matters: An applied study that cites Muntner 2024 (OpenAlex cited-by list) and uses negative-control outcomes before the comparative outcome analysis. An example of the staged pattern in applied work.

short_title: Practical guide to using RWE as primary basis for approval
why_it_matters: Guide covering protocol development, governance and analysis of residual bias for registrational real-world evidence; cites Muntner 2024 (OpenAlex). Shows regulators and sponsors treat governance as part of the design.

short_title: Principled pharmacoepidemiology in the era of RWE
why_it_matters: Review that cites Muntner 2024 (OpenAlex) and lists frameworks for transparent study conduct among the drivers of real-world evidence. Context for the introduction only.

verified_by: Crossref (title and venue only; abstract text not read)
why_it_matters: The title describes an independent committee that handles research hurdles in real time without bias. Evidence that industry teams use a clean-room committee; content not read, so low weight.

Argues that the trial practice of fixing hypotheses, outcomes and analysis in a protocol carries over to observational studies, and discusses when the protocol is set relative to treatment assignment.

Proposes staged access to secondary data: analysts see a subset, register a script, then receive the full data. The closest analogue of a clean room outside pharmacoepidemiology; survey of ALSPAC users.

short_title: Blinding outcomes is neither necessary nor sufficient
why_it_matters: Shows by analysis and simulation that hiding outcomes while choosing matching or propensity scores does not prevent bias when outcomes are predictable from covariates. It bounds what outcome-blindness buys, and is the main caveat for the manuscript.

short_title: For objective causal inference, design trumps analysis
why_it_matters: Already cited in the introduction as the source for changing the design only while the outcome stays unseen.

short_title: Design versus analysis of observational studies
why_it_matters: The first statement of the design-before-outcome principle in the journal the manuscript targets. The bib holds the 2008 paper only (rubin2008).
A trial-design example of adapting a design from baseline covariates without outcomes, with type I error calibration shown by simulation. Low weight.

short_title: A pilot design for observational studies
why_it_matters: Spends a subset of observations, with their outcomes, in the design phase. An alternative to outcome-blind design and a possible way around Fisher's objection; not compatible with withholding the outcome.

short_title: Blind analysis: hide results to seek the truth
why_it_matters: Argues that biology, psychology and the social sciences should adopt the blind analysis used in physics. The source for the sentence on blind analysis in other sciences.

short_title: Blind analysis in nuclear and particle physics
why_it_matters: Review of blind analysis as practised in physics. Older than the search window; cite once, only if the paper mentions physics.

short_title: AHA statement on observational comparative research
why_it_matters: States that a formal protocol should be prepared before every observational study to improve rigor and reduce data manipulation. Supports the first sentence of the introduction.
Reporting guideline for studies that emulate a target trial. Methods already builds the SAP table on its components.

short_title: Reflection paper on RWD in non-interventional studies
why_it_matters: Says the methods for confounding should be prespecified in the protocol or analysis plan, that studies and protocols be registered in the HMA-EMA Catalogue, and that analysis code be public.

short_title: M14 guideline on RWD safety studies
why_it_matters: Says the design, data, methods and analysis should be prespecified in the protocol after the feasibility assessments; in effect in the EU from 18 March 2026. The feasibility it describes concerns whether data sources fit the question, not simulated estimability.

short_title: Preregistration: a key to credible RWE
why_it_matters: States that preregistration is underused and introduces the OSF Real-World Evidence Registry. Supports a sentence on where a locked plan can be deposited.

short_title: Review of tools for target trial studies
why_it_matters: Found 24 tools, 3 of which support the design phase, and no single tool from start to finish. Supports a statement that design-phase software is thin.

verified_by: Agency page opened; PDF text read
why_it_matters: Asks for a prespecified protocol and statistical analysis plan that includes the estimand, an assessment of feasibility and the anticipated operating characteristics. The dossier's simulation tables supply the last two.
Proposes a short statement that reports the protocol, preregistration, data, code and reporting-checklist status of every RWE study. The dossier and lock hash could fill the first two items.
Protocol template for hypothesis-evaluating treatment-effect studies, meant to run from protocol through registration and reporting. The dossier could print a summary that maps onto it.

Preregistration site for real-world studies of treatment effects, hosted on the Open Science Framework; registration returns a URL or DOI. The page does not state a time-stamp rule, so the lock hash would be extra evidence.

short_title: Open science practices in RWE reports
why_it_matters: In 41 articles published from 2019 to October 2024, none cited a preregistered protocol and none met all five open-science items. Evidence that prespecification is rare in practice.

short_title: Commentary on the target trial label
why_it_matters: Argues that observational data cannot reproduce random assignment or blinding, so the label can overstate similarity. A reason to word the manuscript's claims about the trial framework carefully.
Open-access assistant that guides a target trial protocol and warns about misaligned time points. It guides the protocol but does not lock a plan or simulate estimability.
FDA Sentinel process guide for inferential studies on routine-care data; a regulator-side source for fixing design steps before analysis.

short_title: HMA-EMA Catalogues replace EU PAS Register
why_it_matters: The catalogues replaced the ENCePP Resource Database and the EU PAS Register. Relevant if the paper names a European registration route.
Structured template for planning and reporting real-world evidence studies; the companion of HARPER.

short_title: Transparency roadmap of the RWE Transparency Initiative
venue: Value Health 23(9):1128-1136 and Pharmacoepidemiol Drug Saf 29(11):1504-1513
why_it_matters: Recommendations and road map from the initiative that produced the RWE Registry. Background for the registration paragraph.

short_title: Meta-analysis of trial emulations against trials
why_it_matters: Across 107 pairs of observational studies and trials the correlation was 0.59, and 0.83 in the 63 pairs whose design matched the trial more closely. Bounds what a well-designed observational analysis delivers.

In 15 trial emulations, outcome-adaptive LASSO agreed with the trial better than investigator-specified adjustment, and models tuned for treatment prediction alone did poorly. A caution for tuning learners without the outcome.

verified_by: Crossref; PubMed; PMC full text read
why_it_matters: Protocols were registered before the analyses, after feasibility checks and before treatment-stratified outcome counts. Agreement with the trials was higher in the closely emulated subset.
Standardizing to the trial population moved hazard ratios little. Relevant to the point that the estimand's population is part of the design.
Design of a 12-trial benchmarking program that stresses preregistered protocols before initiation and prespecified agreement criteria. Shows the registration practice spreading.
Proposes benchmarking a database study against a trial and then calibrating a second study. A different use of a benchmark; not an outcome-blind step.
Reproduced 150 database studies from the original data sources; most were closely reproduced, and the gaps tracked incomplete reporting.
Report of the first 10 trial emulations in the initiative. Cite only if the paper needs the original reference.

short_title: A plasmode benchmark can refute but not certify
why_it_matters: Argues that a plasmode benchmark can disprove an estimator but not confirm it, and that regenerating treatment from a bounded propensity score avoids the overlap failures that resampling observed treatments causes.

short_title: Negative controls in GLP-1 studies, scoping review
why_it_matters: In 42 studies, none explicitly discussed the assumptions behind the negative-control analysis. Supports listing, by domain, which unmeasured confounders have a control.

Shiny app that runs a plasmode simulation on the user's data to compare estimators for a prespecified ATE. Closest tool to the simulation step. It fixes the estimand, and the repository README asks for an outcome column.

Reports equipoise, balance, minimum detectable relative risk, expected absolute systematic error and generalizability, each with a threshold (defaults 0.2, 0.1, 10, 0.25, off) and a pass, warning or fail; the results table has an unblind flag.
Builds, executes and uploads JSON analysis specifications for HADES modules. Its reference index lists no function that hashes or locks a specification.

short_title: Large-scale propensity scores in small samples
why_it_matters: Standard balance diagnostics failed below about 20,000 patients in this setting, while propensity matching held up at 500. Supports judging estimability by simulation rather than by balance thresholds in small cohorts.

short_title: Tuning LASSO for propensity weighting; synthetic negative controls
why_it_matters: Tunes the propensity model with balance metrics, which need no outcome, and flags residual confounding with synthetic negative-control exposures. Cites both Nance 2024 and Conover 2025 (OpenAlex).

Prespecified diagnostics (minimum detectable relative risk, equipoise, balance, generalizability, expected absolute systematic error) are read before unblinding. The minimum detectable relative risk uses observed outcome event counts; the systematic error uses negative-control outcomes.

Shows that a fixed balance threshold flags chance imbalance in samples near 2,000 and proposes testing whether the standardized difference exceeds the threshold. Relevant to small cohorts such as the four-month Rescue.Co cohort.
Tutorial on plasmode simulation practice and its assumptions, such as representativeness of the sample. Methods citation for the simulation design.

short_title: Undersmoothed LASSO propensity score with targeted learning
why_it_matters: Sentinel-linked work on choosing the degree of undersmoothing; cross-fitting mattered for avoiding non-overlap. A pointer for the learner-defaults item.

Sets out principles for prespecified, systematic evidence generation across a network of databases. The pattern is many questions, one prespecified pipeline; cleanTMLE is one study with a locked plan.

short_title: Plasmode-based bias analysis for unmeasured confounding
why_it_matters: Plasmode simulation used for a quantitative bias analysis on Sentinel data. Related to the wishlist item on a locked bias analysis.
Shows that the CRAN Plasmode 0.1.0 generator mis-aligns exposure probabilities and distorts confounding. A reason not to build on that package.
Overview of how TMLE has been used in FDA submissions and FDA research. Context for why a TMLE-specific design stage matters to regulators.

short_title: Benchmark of observational designs and calibration
verified_by: Crossref (title and venue; abstract read only through a web summary)
why_it_matters: Benchmark that pairs real negative controls with synthetic positive controls and tests empirical calibration. Source for the calibration idea that cleanTMLE does not use.
Workgroup comparing targeted learning with Sentinel propensity-score methods on linked claims and EHR data; status complete. The page names no tool or report.

short_title: Prespecified yet data-adaptive learning in trials
why_it_matters: Picks the TMLE specification by cross-validated variance with sample splitting, tests it with parametric and plasmode simulations, prespecifies the plan and unblinds in real time. The closest published workflow, in randomized trials.

short_title: Causal roadmap and simulations for real-data applications
why_it_matters: Outcome-blind simulations on the study's data structure compare candidate estimators and finalize the statistical analysis plan. The nearest published statement of the design stage; it fixes the estimand first.
Step-by-step choices for a prespecified super learner. Cite in the learner documentation and in the Methods sentence on the library.
Guidance on writing a statistical analysis plan around targeted learning. No abstract was retrievable (not in Crossref or Europe PMC), so read the paper before relying on specifics.
Gives a truncation bound as a function of the sample size, so it needs no outcome. It can enter the plan as one named truncation candidate.
Already cited.

short_title: Guide to selecting among adjustment methods
why_it_matters: Reviews matching, weighting, doubly robust and machine learning methods and gives recommendations for choosing among them. Context for estimator choice.

short_title: Roadmap on Danish registry data, published version
why_it_matters: The bib holds the arXiv version (nanceApplyingCausalRoadmap2023); cite the journal version.
A TMLE design that picks external controls with an outcome-blind matching step (Mertens is an author). An example of an outcome-blind design step inside a TMLE workflow.

short_title: Variable screening in the super learner
why_it_matters: Companion guidance on screening variables before a super learner. Optional for the learner-defaults item.
The roadmap itself; already cited.

short_title: Evaluating and improving RWE with targeted learning
why_it_matters: Applies the roadmap to a published ritodrine study: the data could not identify a dose-response curve, so a simpler contrast was estimated. An example of changing the estimand because the data cannot support it, done after the study.

short_title: Causal roadmap in two safety-monitoring case studies
why_it_matters: Two Sentinel-sponsored case studies that use the roadmap to document analytic decisions. Already cited; the bib entry has no DOI, so add it when the entry is next refreshed.

short_title: Realistic simulations to test TMLE robustness
why_it_matters: Benchmarks TMLE variants on simulations built from ten nutrition-trial datasets with a highly adaptive lasso generator. Precedent for data-based simulation to choose among TMLE variants.
Earlier paper on adaptive prespecification in randomized trials (title). Cite with Balzer 2026.
Already cited.

short_title: Causal estimand selection under positivity violations
why_it_matters: Design-based metrics trade estimator bias against drift from the population of interest. A placeholder in the introduction. It does not simulate outcomes from the design.

short_title: Causal roadmap, targeted learning and TMLE (event page)
verified_by: Event page opened (talk, not a publication)
why_it_matters: Describes outcome-blind simulations to choose the statistical analysis plan and a Sentinel and FDA project on real data. An unpublished effort in the same space; the slides were not available.

short_title: Prioritizing the ATT for drug and device safety
why_it_matters: Argues the ATT should be the default estimand in drug-safety studies and that regulatory guidance says little on estimand choice. Bears on the order of the estimand ladder.

short_title: Tutorial on weighting under positivity violations
why_it_matters: Tutorial that guides choosing a primary target estimand with others as supplementary, and provides the R package ChiPS. A placeholder in the introduction.
Already cited.
